findings_to_judge.finding: CXM's own five prior prints moved +5.96%, -10.00%, +3.05%, +6.05%, -3.03% (close before to close of the print day, all pre-open releases) and the sign is conditioned on the run-in: the only double-digit decline, 2025-09-03, was the print it entered at $8.60 near its 52-week high, which is the same setup as today at $7.94-8.21 after +22.6% in 20 days.

Sprinklr's FY27 non-GAAP operating income guide of $139-141m requires H2 operating income of ~$77-79m against H1 of ~$61.7m (Q1 actual $31.7m plus Q2 guide midpoint $30.0m) — a ~30% step-up in the quarterly run-rate that the CFO justified only as 'improve gradually in the second half of the year as we expect some efficiency gains' — and that FY OI guide had already been cut from $144-146m at the March print.

The Q2 FY27 revenue guide implies professional services of only ~$20.5m (total $214-215m less subscription $193.5-194.5m) versus actual PS of $24.7m, $27.2m and $28.8m in the last three quarters, and Sprinklr beat its own implied PS guide by 25% in Q3 FY26 ($28.8m actual vs $23.0m implied) and 10% in Q1 FY27 ($24.7m vs $22.5m implied) — so a headline revenue beat of roughly 1.5-2.5% is mechanically likely, but at the -10% PS gross margin management guided it adds nothing to operating income.

In the Q1 FY27 10-Q geographic disaggregation, Americas revenue FELL to $112.9m from $117.6m (-4.0% YoY) while 'Other' jumped to $29.6m from $15.9m (+86%), so 48.6% of revenue is now outside the Americas versus 42.8% a year earlier and 44% for FY26 — Sprinklr's home market is contracting and every dollar of growth is coming from the regions where the Middle East disruption and FX sit.

The Q1 FY27 10-Q discloses that 'our operations in the Middle East have been affected by the 2026 Iran conflict, including disruptions to our business activities in the region and inaccessibility, and potential loss, of certain customer data in connection with a third-party data center infrastructure in the United Arab Emirates' and warns of 'significant and unanticipated expenses... emergency data transfers, temporary changes to data processing locations, increased infrastructure costs' — and the conflict's targeting of Gulf data centres was still live in July 2026, i.e. across the whole of the quarter being reported (1 May - 31 July 2026).

The scheduled termination date of Sprinklr's $125m variable-tenor accelerated share repurchase with Citibank is September 1, 2026 — today, the session before the print — after which the dealer's covering purchases (roughly $125m spread over ~115 sessions on a 2.76m-share ADV) stop, and only $75m of the $200m authorization remains through 15 March 2027.

Sprinklr's $125m accelerated share repurchase with Citibank has a stated scheduled termination date of September 1, 2026 - the last session before the print - so the dealer's programmatic buying of roughly 21m shares (about 6-7% of the 2.76m-share ADV every day since 11 March) ends exactly as the event begins; the stock's 54% advance from $5.32 on 1 July to $8.21 on 31 August came in near-daily 1-3% increments with no news gap, and CXM was quoted down 3.3% at $7.94 on 2026-09-01 itself, the ASR's termination date.

The quarter being reported (1 May - 31 July 2026) was run without a Chief Revenue Officer for two of its three months: Scott Millard resigned effective 2025-11-11 after roughly seven weeks in the job, Tom Addis did not start until 2026-07-01, and SVP Global Sales Kevin Connolly left for NewRocket in the same window - so tomorrow's Q3 guide is the first ever set by a revenue chief with two months of tenure.

The Iran-Gulf war, which Sprinklr's 10-Q says caused 'inaccessibility, and potential loss, of certain customer data' at a third-party UAE data centre and which management sized on 4 June as $3-4m of slipped deals plus 54 customers force-migrated to Ireland, escalated again INSIDE the reported quarter (Iranian missiles and drones fired at Gulf states on 2026-07-12) and hostilities resumed on 2026-08-31 - against a guide that assumed 'improvements in the coming quarters', with 44% of FY26 revenue generated outside the Americas.

The 13 August 8-K appointing Microsoft's President of Search & AI, Jordi Ribas, states explicitly that there are no related-party arrangements, family relationships or reportable transactions, and seats him on the Nominating & Corporate Governance and Strategy committees - i.e. it is governance, not a Microsoft commercial relationship - while the same filing shows the board's Strategy Committee was converted from ad hoc to standing at the 2026 annual meeting.
